skill.name: mobile-app-audit
skill.description: Audit mobile apps through code review, device testing, backend checks, and regression verification while preserving the existing design.
skill.summary: Verify mobile bugs and fixes with evidence, impact maps, release checks, and clearly documented testing gaps.
skill.author: ronaldmaco

security_audit.summary: All 95 static findings are false positives involving authorized audit procedures, defensive guidance, public references, or Markdown syntax. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious persistence. Device access and backend probes serve the stated task; writes require explicit approval and test accounts.

finding_verdicts.reason: This paragraph defines production failure analysis and its evidence requirements. It does not direct unrelated system discovery.
The dwarfdump command matches local crash symbols to the affected application build. This is scoped debugging, not host reconnaissance.
Android retrace uses a release mapping file to interpret an application stack trace. No unrelated system information is requested.
The imports support the documented API comparison example. Subsequent requests target the application endpoint rather than an external collection service.
This request sends sample search filters to the application's endpoint for result comparison. No credentials or local files enter the example payload.
urlopen reads the documented search response with a timeout. This implements the requested backend verification rather than data exfiltration.
This is prose about reporting catalog defects and reusing locally saved results. It neither imports Python HTTP libraries nor transmits secrets.
example.com is an illustrative placeholder explicitly labeled as the application's endpoint. It is not an attacker-controlled collection destination.
SMTP sender verification is listed as a possible cause of application failures. No email-sending command, recipient, or message transmission is specified.
The term id refers to catalog identifiers and duplicate data. This line contains no system reconnaissance operation.
The inventory reads project configuration to identify environments and base URLs. SKILL.md forbids printing secrets; unrelated environment files are not requested.
This checks application lifecycle correctness against the target SDK. Process death is a mobile testing condition, not a host discovery instruction.
The checklist tests session persistence across reboot and device locking. It does not extract keychain or keystore credentials.
This requires measured performance baselines and honest reporting of missing measurements. No system discovery command appears here.
The commands measure launch time for the application under test. Their package and activity scope matches the declared performance audit.
gfxinfo and profiling commands measure application frame performance. They do not enumerate unrelated systems or collect credentials.
Memory sampling and leak inspection are scoped to repeated application navigation. This is ordinary performance diagnosis.
The UI hierarchy dump supports accessibility label and target-size checks on the test device. It is not unrelated system reconnaissance.
The commands capture test screenshots and UI elements. /dev/tty is the hierarchy output destination, not a sensitive file being extracted.
This is an authentication scenario list covering signup, login, reset, and logout. It contains no configuration-library or environment access.
Screen capture and UI element inspection provide evidence for application tests. Their purpose is visible-state verification, not host profiling.
The optional device tool lists supported testing capabilities and runs its own diagnostics. This is documented setup, not covert system reconnaissance.
Device size, text scale, and network settings simulate accessibility and slow-device conditions. The commands serve the stated application testing scenario.
/dev/null discards input and diagnostic output during a TLS certificate expiry check. It is not a source of sensitive data.
The checks inspect certificate expiry and signing metadata for the audited application. They do not export private keys or send keystore contents elsewhere.
This points readers to Android and Apple release notes. It requests documentation review, not system discovery.
TLS and signing-certificate metadata establish application expiry risks. The targets are application hosts and signing artifacts, not unrelated infrastructure.
The grep searches application source for dates and expiring feature logic. It performs no system or network enumeration.
The report template records regression tests and manual case identifiers. The word id does not invoke a system command.
Finding identifiers connect coverage rows to report entries. This is report formatting, not reconnaissance.

The .well-known paths are public app-link verification documents. Checking them does not access hidden local files.
curl redirects response bodies to /dev/null while retaining status codes. No sensitive device file is read.
These variables identify the application's backend for authorization checks. No embedded credential string or external secret destination is present.

Private keys and payment secrets are examples of material that must not ship in an application. No actual secret or extraction instruction appears.

aapt2, bundletool, and apksigner inspect the application's release artifact for unsafe flags. They are ordinary build inspection tools.

File enumeration is limited to the application's simulator container or debug sandbox. It checks storage cleanup across authentication states.

content.user_title: Audit Mobile Apps and Verify Fixes with Evidence
content.value_statement: Mobile bugs can persist across accounts, devices, backend data, and release builds. This skill guides evidence-based audits and verifies fixes across affected paths.
actual_capabilities: Structure bug verification, fix verification, targeted audits, full audits, store checks, production postmortems, and future-risk reviews.
Trace failures from UI state through requests, backend data, persistence, and rendering using impact maps.
Compare application results with API responses and inspect catalog integrity, CDN behavior, and authorization controls.
Guide device testing for lifecycle changes, slow networks, accessibility, performance, and first-time user flows.
Propose minimal fixes with approval, add regression tests, and verify affected consumers and sibling platforms.
Produce evidence-backed findings, coverage tables, delivery checklists, and dated future-risk assessments.
limitations: This is an agent workflow, not a standalone scanner or a guarantee that every defect will be found.
Builds and device checks require installed toolchains, usable signing, and access to suitable devices or simulators.
Backend verification requires authorized access and test accounts; write tests require explicit approval.
Store rules and future deadlines require current official sources; unavailable evidence must remain unverified.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Persistent Mobile Bug
use_cases.description: Reproduce a reported failure, trace its cause, and verify the fix across accounts, saved state, and affected screens.

use_cases.title: Verify Release Quality
use_cases.description: Check release builds, critical flows, accessibility, backend reachability, and store readiness while recording testing gaps.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production Failures
use_cases.description: Match crash evidence to the exact build, reconstruct the incident timeline, and identify regression tests and prevention work.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Reported Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this mobile bug: [steps, expected result, actual result]. Ask for missing build details, reproduce it, and report evidence without changing code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: turn a user complaint into a reproducible test case.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Claimed Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the fix in [commit] for [bug]. Compare the reported scenario and affected consumers, run regressions, and distinguish code changes from released fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: confirm a fix before closing a ticket.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [app] for release across [platforms]. Use test accounts, check critical flows and current official store rules, and record coverage. Request approval before changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate application, backend, and submission checks.

prompt_templates.title: Reconstruct an Incident and Assess Future Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [incident] using [build, crash report, telemetry]. Reconstruct the timeline and impact map. Assess related 12-month risks with dated official sources. Propose fixes for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: connect production evidence, regression coverage, and upcoming platform changes.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: verify why selecting a venue shows unrelated events.
output: Finding: the selected venue is omitted from the request, so results are unfiltered.
Evidence: compare the recorded request parameters with the API response and visible results.
Impact map: check the filter sheet, chips, saved preferences, and sibling platform.
Status: report the cause as suspected until evidence is collected; do not change code without approval.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: assess whether a corrected login flow is ready to ship.
output: Coverage: verify fresh login, expired sessions, offline retry, app restart, and the release configuration.
Evidence: attach test results and before-and-after observations for each affected path.
Delivery: distinguish a passing local build from a released store build and deployed backend.
Open items: list unavailable device checks as not tested rather than passed.

best_practices: Provide exact steps, application version and build, device, account state, region, and expected behavior before testing.
Use owned systems and test accounts; approve writes explicitly and keep secrets out of reports.
Require evidence for each affected path and verify the release build before closing the issue.
anti_patterns: Treating a code change or successful debug build as proof that users received a fix.
Hiding invalid selections or silently broadening a request instead of addressing the cause.
Running write probes without approval or reporting untested coverage as passed.

faq.question: Which mobile stacks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It provides checks for native iOS, Android, Flutter, and React Native or Expo, with tooling adapted to the project.

faq.question: Does it run as a standalone testing tool?
faq.answer: No. An AI agent follows the workflow using file access, a shell, and available development tools.

faq.question: Can it work without a simulator or device?
faq.answer: It can review code and authorized backend behavior. Device-dependent checks must remain not tested until suitable access is available.

faq.question: Will it change the application design?
faq.answer: The workflow preserves layout, copy, and navigation. It proposes minimal fixes and requires approval before making changes.

faq.question: Can it test production backends?
faq.answer: Checks are limited to the owner's systems. Writes require explicit approval and a test environment when available; use test accounts.

faq.question: Does it guarantee store approval or complete security coverage?
faq.answer: No. It documents evidence and gaps, checks current official requirements, and separates suspected issues from verified findings.
